summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of severe Crohn’s disease, status post multiple abdominal surgeries including colectomy and ileostomy takedown, was admitted with acute abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. The presentation was consistent with a Crohn’s flare, likely triggered by recent discontinuation of prednisone. Infection was ruled out with negative blood, stool, and urine cultures. Imaging showed no obstruction. A flexible sigmoidoscopy confirmed active inflammation in the rectosigmoid and ileum, with biopsy findings of chronic active ileitis. He was treated with IV solumedrol, transitioned to oral prednisone, and started on hydrocortisone enemas. Acute kidney injury due to dehydration resolved with IV fluids. His pain and diarrhea improved, and he was discharged on a prednisone taper, enemas, and short-term pain medication with follow-up arranged with gastroenterology.
